primarySource.paper: Pratt, Robles, Zaharescu, Zeindler, 'More than five-twelfths of the zeros of zeta are on the critical line', arXiv:1802.10521, Res. Math. Sci. 7 (2020) - pulled 2026-11-11
primarySource.theorem4_1: the twisted second moment I(alpha,beta) = int zeta(1/2+alpha+it) zeta(1/2+beta+it) |sum_{d<=N} a_d d^{-(1/2+it)}|^2 Phi(t/T) dt, N = T^theta, theta < 1, alpha,beta << L^-1, is computed unconditionally with explicit main term plus error E by coefficient regime:

regimes.saturation: theta < 17/33 (first term: 33theta/20 + 3/20 < 1; second term slack: theta/2 + 1/2 < 1 fails only at theta > 2)
regimes.ingredient: Bettin, Chandee and Radziwill, the trilinear Kloosterman sum (improvement of Duke-Friedlander-Iwaniec due to Bettin and Chandee) - the paper says the 17/33 - eps best bound for arbitrary coefficients is DUE to them

regimes.saturation: theta < 6/11 (both terms saturate: 11theta/6 = 1 and 11theta/12 + 1/2 = 1 at theta = 6/11)
regimes.note: consistent with the 2017 Pratt-Robles 'Perturbed moments and a longer mollifier' (arXiv:1706.04593) which increased the Feng-mollifier length from theta < 17/33 to theta < 6/11

regimes.coefficients: (mu * Lambda_1^{*k1} * ... * Lambda_D^{*kD})(n) - the DEGREE-D family, CONTAINING the classical Levinson coefficients mu(n) at D = 0
regimes.saturation: theta < 4/7 (BOTH terms saturate simultaneously: 7theta/4 = 1 and 7theta/8 + 1/2 = 1 at theta = 4/7)
regimes.verbatim: the proof states: 'Thus, taking N = T^{4/7-eps} is permissible.'

primarySource.errorStructure: Type I: summation by parts + the Weil bound for incomplete Kloosterman sums; Type II: bilinear Kloosterman sums via Deshouillers-Iwaniec Lemma 1 with the balance W = U^{1/4}; the combined bound carries the exponents 7/4 (Case 3), 33/20 (Case 1), 11/6 (Case 2) - the bilinear Kloosterman-sum estimates ARE the source of the exponents
primarySource.bchb917: section 1.3 verbatim: 'Balasubramanian, Conrey and Heath-Brown examined the error terms from the mean value integral in (1.2) and the resulting exponential sums. In particular they showed using Vaughan's identity on 1/zeta(s) and Weil's bound for Kloosterman sums that one could push the size of the length theta past the 1/2 barrier to 9/17 when the coefficients are given by (1.3)' with (1.3) b_C(n,y) = mu(n) n^{sigma0 - 1/2} P(log(y/n)/log y), P real polynomial, P(0) = 0, P(1) = 1
primarySource.openQuestion: section 9 item 4 verbatim: 'Moreover, it would also be interesting to set d = 1 and analyze how a large truncation of l could yield terms from a higher degree d >= 2. What would be a good balance between the degree d and the truncation l?'
